# Producer engine

<!-- Generated by `npm run generate:engine-doc -w @clossys/producer` from `src/engine/`. Do not edit by hand; engine/doc.test.ts fails when this file and the code differ. -->

Every record write of a consumer workspace goes through one engine: it appends one event to a hash-chained, append-only log, under one lock per workspace, and keeps a derived index that is never the source of truth. Files only, no database. The record files themselves (slots, candidates, pins, ledgers, queue entries, requests, library versions, run records) stay where and how they are; the events name them by path and sha256.

## Files

Paths are relative to the workspace root (the folder that holds `clossys/`).

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `clossys/.state/events.jsonl` | the event log: one JSON event per line, append-only, each line chained to the one before |
| `clossys/.state/engine.lock` | the engine lock: created with O_EXCL, holds `{ pid, host, at, token }` of its writer |
| `clossys/.state/index.json` | the derived index, rebuilt from the log plus the records |

Records under `clossys/agents/<director|designer|writer|publisher|producer>/` and `clossys/library/` log to the workspace that holds them. `clossys/.state` (the consumer-layout contract's `stateDir`) holds only machine files, beside the records in `clossys/`; a root `.clossys/` fails `clossys check --engine` and `clossys migrate state --apply` moves it in.

## Types

`src/engine/types.ts` holds each type and its runtime validator (`eventIssues`, `stepIssues`, `runIssues`, `attestationIssues`, `gateIssues`, `draftIssues`).

### EngineEvent

| Field | Rule |
|---|---|
| `schema` | "clossys.event/1" |
| `seq` | integer from 0, one more than the previous line |
| `prev` | sha256 of the previous line's bytes; GENESIS (64 zeros) on line 0 |

| `inputs` | [{ path, sha256 }]: workspace-relative POSIX paths, sorted and unique; sha256 null when the file is absent |
| `id` | sha256 of the line's canonical JSON without id |

## The chain

Line n carries `seq` n and `prev`, the sha256 of line n-1's bytes (line 0: `GENESIS`, 64 zeros). Its `id` is the sha256 of its canonical JSON without `id`. `verifyChain(root)` reads the whole log and reports:

| Issue | When |
|---|---|
| `malformed` | a line is not JSON or not an event |
| `torn` | the file does not end with a newline (an interrupted append) |
| `edit` | a line no longer hashes to its own id, or the next line's prev is not its hash |
| `gap` | a seq is higher than the line before it plus one (a line was removed) |
| `reorder` | a seq is not higher than the line before it (lines were moved or duplicated) |

Removing lines from the end leaves a valid shorter chain; the index head is what notices it.

## The one writer

`appendEvent(root, draft)` validates the draft, takes the engine lock, chains the event to the last line, appends it as one line (fsync) and updates the index, all under the lock. It writes nothing on an invalid draft (EngineEventError), a torn or invalid last line (EngineLogError) or a busy lock (EngineBusyError). `recordEvent(paths, draft)` is the call a record writer makes after it wrote its files: the root comes from the first path, the inputs are every path with the sha256 of its bytes now. Since its files are already on disk, any failure of that append (a busy lock past the wait, a torn log) is a RecordCommittedError (code `RECORD_COMMITTED`), never an EngineBusyError: the write is done and must not be retried. The loop runner's own events (`commitEvent`) and a transaction's commit refuse the same way.

A record write under a slot-record lock is one transaction of events (`deferEvents(write)`): its events are held and appended in order when the write returns. A write its guard refuses puts its files back and drops the held events that name them, so a refused write logs nothing and the log never names bytes that are gone. A write that throws without undoing keeps its events. A scope opened inside another joins the outer one, so its events append when the outermost write returns.

An agent step of a loop is judged by what it changed: the log may change only by a pure append that verifies on the chain, and the index only to its rebuild (`engineLogIssue` and `engineIndexIssue`, loop/agent-snapshot.ts). Each new event is either the step's own (a kind its decider verb makes, by the step's agent or the Producer code that verb runs, never an owner, a planner or another agent: `AGENT_STEP_EVENTS`) naming only files the step changed, each by the sha256 of its bytes; or the runner's run.state event for the run's own state file, by its bytes. A forged approval line chains as well as a real one, so the chain alone never clears it.

### Lock

| Rule | Value |
|---|---|
| create | `open(lock, "wx")`: exactly one writer creates it |
| wait for a live holder | 5000 ms, then EngineBusyError (code `ENGINE_BUSY`) naming the holder; nothing is written |
| stale: same host | the owner pid is no longer alive |
| stale: another host | held longer than 15 min |
| stale: no readable owner | older than 60 s |
| takeover | read the stale lock instance (its bytes, device, inode and mtime from one open), create that instance's own recovery marker (O_EXCL, named by a hash of the instance), re-read and re-judge the lock under the marker, then rename a fresh lock over it: the lock file is never absent, and only the one process holding the marker of the exact instance it judged replaces it; a marker whose owner died is itself recovered the same way |
| release | only while the lock still carries the holder's token |
| order | a writer takes its record lock (slot, agent, entry) first and the engine lock last |

Limit of the stale rule: staleness is judged by pid, host and age, never by asking the holder. A second writer is possible only when a live holder is judged stale under these time rules: a writer on another host still holding the lock after 15 min (or seen that old through clock skew between the hosts), a writer on another machine that reports the same host name (its pid is not alive here), or a live writer whose lock still has no readable owner after 60 s. No other path admits two writers.

## Writers

Each wired writer keeps its on-disk record and adds one event per write.

| Event kind | Writer | Subject |
|---|---|---|
| `<slot\|agent>.<op>` | `packages/producer/src/records/slot-write.ts` | <agent>[/<slot>]: one per ledger event, op from the ledger op |
| `<slot\|agent>.backfill` | `packages/producer/src/records/slot-write.ts` | <agent>[/<slot>]: a ledger rewritten by the ledger migration |
| `pin.probe-repoint / pin.probe-restore` | `packages/producer/src/records/slot-write.ts` | designer/<slot>: the theme probe's pin swap and its restore |
| `migration.record` | `packages/producer/src/records/slot-write.ts` | migration:<id> |
| `<pin kind>.write` | `packages/producer/src/records/pin.ts` | <agent>/<slot>: a pin or pin-map document |
| `request.create / request.write` | `packages/producer/src/records/request.ts` | request:<id> |
| `queue.create / queue.replace` | `packages/producer/src/queue/entry.ts` | <queue>/<entry id>: every queue entry write, the chat answer path included |
| `library.version` | `packages/producer/src/records/library.ts` | library:<slot>/<element>/v<n> |
| `dependency.add` | `packages/producer/src/records/adopt-dependencies.ts` | designer/<slot>: the code adopt's package.json and package-lock.json after it declared and installed its stock item's dependencies |
| `run.state / run.record / run.settle / pin.revert` | `packages/producer/src/loop/runner.ts` | loop:<loop>/<run id>: run state, the run's ledger record, a settle record (a fixed-rule code step that settled or passed on an agent step), a reverted pin |
| `state.migrate` | `packages/producer/src/engine/migrate-state.ts` | state:<state dir>: a legacy root state folder moved into the state folder, its logged records named at both paths |
| `run.queue` | `packages/producer/src/loop/runner.ts` | loop:loop.fill/<run id>: one fill queue entry of the T1 init, the leaf's slot.json its input (FILL-PRELUDE D1) |

## Derived index

| Field | What |
|---|---|
| `schema` | "clossys.index/1" |
| `events` | how many lines the log holds |
| `head` | sha256 of the log's last line (null when empty): a removed tail line changes it |
| `subjects` | { <subject>: { seq, kind, actor, at } } of the last event about each subject |
| `records` | { <path>: { seq, logged, disk } }: the last event naming each file, the sha256 it logged and the sha256 of the file on disk now |

The index is never the source of truth: `appendEvent` keeps it current, a rebuild writes it from scratch, and `clossys check --engine` fails when the stored index differs from a rebuild or a record's bytes differ from the sha256 its last event logged.

## Verbs

| Verb | What |
|---|---|
| `clossys index --rebuild` | rewrite clossys/.state/index.json from the log plus the records, under the engine lock; exit 1 when the chain does not verify |
| `clossys index` | compare the stored index with a rebuild (read-only); exit 1 when they differ |
| `clossys check --engine` | verifyChain, index agreement, record drift and the consumer layout (no root .clossys/ beside clossys/.state/) on a consumer workspace; exit 1 on any issue |
| `clossys migrate state [--apply\|--check]` | move a root .clossys/ into clossys/.state/ under the engine lock and log one state.migrate event; a dry run unless --apply; --check exits 1 while one exists |
| `clossys check --side-door` | the engine.side-door scan of a checkout (packages/<producer\|designer\|writer\|publisher\|director>/{src,bin,scripts} and scripts/); exit 1 on any finding |

## Check engine.side-door

Rule R-ENGINE-SIDE-DOOR. A static scan of `packages/<producer|designer|writer|publisher|director>/{src,bin,scripts} and scripts/` for writes to `clossys/.state/**` (or `.clossys/**`) or to a slot record outside the engine API. It fails on every finding of the rules stated below. No allowlist and no baseline. Excluded: test files (`*.test.*`, `*.spec.*`), declaration files (`*.d.ts`) and folders named `node_modules`, `__fixtures__`, `__tests__`, `__golden__`, `fixtures` at any depth. Build output at a package root (`dist`, `build`) is outside the scanned folders; a `build` folder inside `src` is source and is scanned.

What each rule flags, and nothing more. The scan parses the files ending in `.mjs`, `.cjs`, `.js`, `.jsx`, `.ts`, `.tsx`, `.mts`, `.cts` with the TypeScript compiler and reads the shell and hook files (`.sh`, `.bash`, `.zsh`, and extensionless files that are executable or start with `#!`) line by line; no other file is read. `write` and `sink`: a write call (the write calls listed below, or an open with a write flag), or a call to a write wrapper, outside the engine API, whose path argument the scan resolves through taint to an engine or slot-record path: a path string, a slot-model path helper, or a name, return value or constant derived from one, within the file or through imports and re-exports. `exec`: a child-process call (`exec`, `execSync`, `execFile`, `execFileSync`, `spawn`, `spawnSync`, `fork`) of `child_process` bound by a named, renamed, default or namespace import, `import ... = require`, `require`, `createRequire` or `import()`, or a name bound to one of these, outside the engine API, where an argument names a state folder (`clossys/.state` or `.clossys`) or a slot path literally, through the string fold, or through taint. `shell`: a line of one of those shell or hook files that names a state folder or a slot path. `script` and `unpaired`: as the table says. Any write not matched by these rules is not seen by this check.

| Finding | Means |
|---|---|
| `write` | writes an engine or slot-record path outside the engine API |
| `sink` | hands an engine or slot-record path to a write wrapper outside the engine API |
| `script` | a script calls a record writer directly; run the clossys verb instead |
| `unpaired` | uses a slot-model file primitive in a file that appends no ledger event, so no engine event names the write |
| `exec` | runs a child process whose arguments name a state folder or a slot-record path; the command is not parsed, so its writes bypass the engine API |
| `shell` | a shell or hook file names a state folder or a slot-record path; its writes bypass the engine API |

Write calls: `writeFileSync`, `writeFile`, `appendFileSync`, `appendFile`, `unlinkSync`, `unlink`, `mkdirSync`, `mkdir`, `rmSync`, `rm`, `rmdirSync`, `rmdir`, `renameSync`, `rename`, `copyFileSync`, `copyFile`, `cpSync`, `cp`, `createWriteStream`, `symlinkSync`, `symlink`, `linkSync`, `link`, `truncateSync`, `truncate`, `utimesSync`, `utimes`, `chmodSync`, `chmod`, and an open with a write flag.

The engine API (writes here log events):

| File | Functions | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `packages/producer/src/engine/` | all | the event log, its lock and its derived index |
| `packages/producer/src/records/slot-write.ts` | writes inside withDirLock, slotLocked, agentLocked, deferEvents; replaceModelFile, createModelFile, removeModelFile, moveModelEntry, dropEmptyModelDir, withDirLock | the slot-model writer, per call: a write inside a record transaction (withDirLock, slotLocked, agentLocked, deferEvents), whose ledger event it logs, or in a paired slot-model primitive or the lock itself |
| `packages/producer/src/records/pin.ts` | writePinDoc | pin and pin-map documents |
| `packages/producer/src/records/request.ts` | writeRequest, createRequest | work requests (queue-entry/2) |
| `packages/producer/src/records/library.ts` | writeElementVersion | element library versions |
| `packages/producer/src/queue/entry.ts` | createQueueEntry, replaceQueueEntry | queue entries, the answer write path |
| `packages/producer/src/loop/runner.ts` | writeLedger, revertPin, saveState, logRun | loop run records, the run state and the run's pin revert |

Record writers a script must not call directly: `appendEvent`, `recordEvent`, `writePinDoc`, `writeRequest`, `writeElementVersion`, `createQueueEntry`, `replaceQueueEntry`, `writeCandidate`, `writeCandidateBytes`, `writePin`, `writeConfirm`, `writeNotNeeded`, `writeTargetDecision`, `writeTargetConfirm`, `writeTargetNotNeeded`, `writeSeatDecision`, `writeVerdict`, `writeReissue`, `writeCritique`, `writeSlotSeed`, `writeSlotOptions`, `writeSyncedSlot`, `replaceModelFile`, `createModelFile`, `removeModelFile`, `moveModelEntry`.

Slot-model file primitives (`replaceModelFile`, `createModelFile`, `removeModelFile`, `moveModelEntry`, `dropEmptyModelDir`) must be paired in the same file with a ledger appender (`appendIaEvent`, `appendSlotDocEvent`, `appendRetireCandidate`, `appendRetireSlot`, `appendCraftEvent`, `appendMigrationEvents`, `writeSeatDecision`).
